proof_audit.claim: Screening decision and value of information
proof_audit.audit: Defines physical success probability, zero funding rate, risk neutrality, lend/refuse choice and two-state loan payoff. Uses conditional independence of signal and success given type before combining quality posteriors. Solves the linear funding threshold including thresholds outside the unit interval, with a stated refusal tie. Total expectation and the pointwise positive-part inequalities prove gross signal value weakly exceeds the best untested decision. Zero-mass branches are excluded from conditional expectations. Test costs are charged to all applicants and net information value compared against the best no-test policy. No welfare or no-arbitrage conclusion is inferred.

Limited-liability debt and borrower residual cash are explicit. The intervention removes the private benefit before the action decision, so the prudent and diversion payoffs change from18/20 to18/12. Direct claimants share the debt benefit but the intervention cost is borne individually. The no-enforcement equilibrium is proved only in the post-funding game; the financing decision separately includes principal, enforcement and delegation cost. Six-claimant exactly-one-enforcer best replies, the private-benefit tie, and the delegation-cost cap are taught and fully solved. Verifiable completion/conditional payment is an explicit assumed commitment technology, not a theorem that banking solves all agency problems.

proof_audit.claim: Deposit creation, consolidation and income cash
proof_audit.audit: Every loan and settlement entry independently balances. Loan36 increases A loans/deposits without reserves or equity; payment24 transfers both reserves and deposit balances from A to B. System reserves remain40 and system deposits rise only on origination. The5 payment probe is exactly after settlement and before later receipts; it is not posted as negative cash. The later income ledger is only A with external counterparties, excluding the failed probe. Confirmed loss5 with no allowance changes loans/equity and not cash. The profit2, finalcash7 and earliergap5 refer to distinct quantities and dates. Ratios state one-year units and arithmetic opening/closing denominators; they are not regulatory ratios. External equity, external borrowing and conversion of an existing deposit are distinguished transaction by transaction.

proof_audit.claim: Feasible liquidity insurance and withdrawal thresholds
proof_audit.audit: Defines a nonatomic population of mass100, known early share, private types, date0 investment, divisible liquidation, storage, utility at zero, mutually owned residual distribution and no outside funding/insurance/suspension. Queue ranks are uniform and formed after withdrawal decisions. Early-only withdrawal pays1.1 and leaves1.45 for late types; separate early and late deviations establish a no-run equilibrium. The chosen reciprocal utility is increasing/strictly concave and its expected-utility improvement over direct holding is computed exactly. At baseline liquidation1, direct all-long holding is an autarky optimum given no trade; at lower liquidation it is only a comparison plan. No global contract optimum is claimed. Budget accounting yields c2(w), capacity and the indifference threshold; differentiation and a strict inequality establish monotonicity and threshold ordering.

When other claimants run, their requests exceed liquidation resources, and an atomless late deviation leaves zero residual resources. Joining receives1.1 with probability10/11, otherwise0; expected utility-5/3 is compared with waiting utility-10, rather than utility of average proceeds. The early-type deviation is also checked. Full-run waiter mean is undefined and returned as null; the separate hypothetical-deviation value is explicitly zero. The manuscript does not infer date0 participation, run selection, finite-large-depositor behavior or the effects of insurance from this conditional game.
